artifacts.rationale: LoF is strongly associated with lower HDL, total cholesterol, and lipoproteins (p < 1e-33). However, evidence is limited to biomarkers; no hard clinical endpoints are present in the data.
The gene is highly tolerant of loss-of-function: pLI is near 0, LOEUF is high (1.07), and it is not essential in any DepMap cell lines.
Loss of function (LoF) is linked to 17 diseases across genetic, cancer, immune, hematologic, and musculoskeletal categories. GWAS/burden signals show strong pleiotropy in blood cell traits.

challenges.rationale: The rationale explicitly states the evidence is biomarker-only with no hard clinical endpoints.
The rationale admits that no non-European (non-EUR) data was shown.
The associations are limited to LDL and total cholesterol measurements rather than clinical disease endpoints.
Safety claims LoF causes multiple Mendelian diseases, which contradicts the high LoF tolerance (LOEUF > 1, pLI ~ 0) reported in A4.
The rationale confirms evidence is limited to biomarkers with no hard clinical endpoints present.
The claim of 17 LoF-linked diseases contradicts the extremely high tolerance metrics (pLI 0, LOEUF 1.07) and lack of cell essentiality in A6.

artifacts.rationale: Strong LoF burden signals for lower HDL/cholesterol are biomarker-only, EUR-centric, and now countered by safety reports of LoF associations with 17 diseases, suggesting net harm.
Mendelian LoF associations in cancer and immune categories persist, but high tolerance metrics (pLI 0, LOEUF 1.07) suggest these risks may be less severe or penetrant than initially estimated.
